elements.name: Changeling
elements.desc: Long ago there was a woman named Jes, and she had one hundred children. Her rivals conspired against her and swore to kill her children. Jes begged the...

elements.name: Change Appearance
elements.desc:
As an action, you can transform your appearance or revert to your natural form. You can't duplicate the appearance of a creature you've never seen, and you revert to your natural form if you die.

You decide what you look like, including your height, weight, facial features, the sound of your voice, coloration, hair length, sex, and any other distinguishing characteristics. You can make yourself appear as a member of another race, though none of your game statistics change. You also can't appear as a creature of a different size than you, and your basic shape stays the same; if you're bipedal, you can't use this trait to become quadrupedal, for instance. Your clothing and other equipment don't change in appearance, size, or shape to match your new form, requiring you to keep a few extra outfits on hand to make the most compelling disguise possible

Even to the most astute observers, your ruse is usually indiscernible. If you rouse suspicion, or if a wary creature suspects something is amiss, you have advantage on any Charisma (Deception) check you make to avoid detection.

elements.name: Changeling Instincts
elements.desc: You gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Deception, Insight, Intimidation, or Persuasion.

elements.name: Unsettling Visage
elements.desc:
When a creature you can see makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the roll. You must use this feature before knowing whether the attack hits or misses.

Using this trait reveals your shapeshifting nature to any creature within 30 feet that can see you. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

elements.name: Divergent Persona
elements.desc: You gain proficiency with one tool of your choice. Define a persona associated with that proficiency: establish the name, race, gender, age, and other details. While you are in the form of this persona, the related proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses that proficiency.

elements.name: Kalashtar
elements.desc: I am klashtar, born of two worlds. Over a thousand years ago, my ancestor bound her bloodline to the spirit Kashtai, and I am a child of that union. Kashtai...

elements.name: Dual Mind
elements.desc: When you make a wisdom saving throw, you can use your reaction to gain advantage on the roll. You can use this trait immediately before or after you roll, but before any of the roll's effects occur.

elements.name: Mental Discipline
elements.desc: You have resistance to psychic damage.

elements.name: Mind Link
elements.desc:
You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet of you. You don't need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your telepathic messages, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic itself.

As a bonus action when you're speaking telepathically to a creature, you can give that creature the ability to speak telepathically to you until the start of your next turn. To use this ability, the creature must be within 60 feet of you and be able to see you.

elements.name: Psychic Glamour
elements.desc: Choose one of the following skills; Insight, Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. You have advantage on all ability checks you make with that skill.

elements.name: Psychic Glamour (Insight)
elements.desc: You have advantage on Insight checks.

elements.name: Psychic Glamour (Intimidation)
elements.desc: You have advantage on Intimidation checks.

elements.name: Psychic Glamour (Performance)
elements.desc: You have advantage on Performance checks.

elements.name: Psychic Glamour (Persuasion)
elements.desc: You have advantage on Persuasion checks.

elements.name: Severed from Dreams
elements.desc: Kalashtar sleep, but they don't connect to the plane of dreams as other creatures do. Instead, their minds draw from the memories of their otherworldly spirit while they sleep. As such, you are immune to spells and other magical effects that require you to dream, like the dream spell, but not to spells and effects that put you to sleep, like the sleep spell.

elements.name: Shifter
elements.desc: Geth’s ancient heritage rose up from deep within him, spreading out from the core of his being. Some shifters manifested terrible claws, massive fangs,...

elements.name: Keen Senses
elements.desc: You have proficiency with the Perception skill.

elements.name: Shifting
elements.desc:
As a bonus action, you can assume a more bestial appearance. This transformation lasts for 1 minute, until you die, or until you revert to your normal appearance as a bonus action. When you shift, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) temporary hitpoits. You also gain additional benefits that depend on your shifter subrace, described below.

Once you shift, you can’t do so again until you fininsh a short or long rest.

elements.name: Beasthide Shifter
elements.desc: Stoic and solid, a beasthide shifter draws strength and stability from the beast within. Beasthide shifters are typically tied to the bear or the boar, but...

elements.name: Tough
elements.desc: You have proficiency with the Athletics skill.

elements.name: Shifting Feature (Beasthide Shifter)
elements.desc: Whenever you shift, you gain 1d6 additional temporary hit points, and while shifted, you have a +1 bonus to your AC.

elements.name: Longtooth Shifter
elements.desc: Longtooth shifters are fierce and aggressive, but they form deep bonds with their friends. Many longtooth shifters have canine traits that become more...

elements.name: Fierce
elements.desc: You have proficiency with the Intimidation skill.

elements.name: Shifting Feature (Longtooth Shifter)
elements.desc: While shifted, you can use your elongated fangs to make an unarmed strike as a bonus action. If you hit with your fangs, you can deal piercing damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

elements.name: Swiftstride Shifter
elements.desc: Swiftstride shifters are graceful and quick. Typically feline in nature, swiftstride shifteres are often aloof and difficult to pin down physically or socially.

elements.name: Graceful
elements.desc: You have proficiency with the Acrobatics skill.

elements.name: Swift Stride
elements.desc: Your walking speed increases by 5 feet.

elements.name: Shifting Feature (Swiftstride Shifter)
elements.desc: While shifted, your walking speed increases by an additional 5 feet. Additionally, you can move up to 10 feet as a reaction when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

elements.name: Wildhunt Shifter
elements.desc: Wildhunt shifters are sharp and insightful. Some are constantly alert, ever wary for possible threats. Others focus on their intuition, searching within....

elements.name: Natural Tracker
elements.desc: You have proficiency with the Survival skill.

elements.name: Mark the Scent
elements.desc: As a bonus action, you can mark one creature you can see within 10 feet of you. Until the end of your next long rest, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make to find the marked create, and you always know the location of that creature if it is within 60 feet of you. You can’t use this trait again until you finish a short or long rest.

elements.name: Shifting Feature (Wildhunt Shifter)
elements.desc: While shifted, you have advantage on Wisdom checks.

elements.name: Warforged
elements.desc: “Pierce was built by design, while you were built by accident,” Lakashtai said. “The soul is what matters, not the shape of the vessel.”

elements.name: Warforged Resilience
elements.desc:
You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits:

- You have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned, and you have resistance to poison damage.
- You are immune to disease.
- You don’t need to eat, drink, or breathe.
- You don’t need to sleep and don’t suffer the effects of exhaustion due to lack of rest, and magic can’t put you to sleep.

elements.name: Sentry’s Rest
elements.desc: When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn’t render you unconscious, and you can see and hear as normal.

elements.name: Integrated Protection
elements.desc:
Your body has built-in defensive layers, which determine your armor class. You gain no benefit from wearing armor, but if you are using a shield, you apply its bonus as normal.

You can alter your body to enter different defensive modes; each time you finish a long rest rest, choose one mode to adopt from the Integrated Protection table, provided you meet the mode’s prerequisite.

INTEGRATED PROTECTION

Mode | Prerequisite | Effect
Darkwood Core (unarmored) | None | 11 + your Dexterity modifier (add proficiency bonus if proficiency with light armor)
Composite Plating (armor) | Medium armor proficiency | 13 + your Dexterity modifier (maximum of 2) + your proficiency bonus.
Heavy Plating (armor) | Heavy armor proficiency | 16 + your proficiency bonus; disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

elements.name: Darkwood Core
elements.desc: Armor Class. 11 + your Dexterity modifier (add proficiency bonus if proficiency with light armor)

elements.name: Composite Plating
elements.desc:
Prerequisite: Medium armor proficiency

Armor Class. 13 + your Dexterity modifier (maximum of 2) + your proficiency bonus.

elements.name: Heavy Plating
elements.desc:
Prerequisite: Heavy armor proficiency

Armor Class. 16 + your proficiency bonus; disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

elements.name: Specialized Design
elements.desc: You gain one skill proficiency of your choice, one tool proficiency of your choice, and fluency in one language of your choice.

elements.name: Integrated Tool
elements.desc: Choose one tool you’re proficient with. This tool is integrated into your body, and you double your proficiency bonus for any ability checks you make with it. You must have your hands free to use this integrated tool.

elements.name: Juggernaut Warforged
elements.desc: You’re an imposing war machine built for close combat and raw might. You tower over your comrades; juggernaut warforged stand between 6 and 7 feet in height...

elements.name: Iron Fists
elements.desc: When you make an unarmed strike, you can deal 1d4 + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage instead of the normal damage.

elements.name: Powerful Build
elements.desc: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

elements.name: Skirmisher Warforged
elements.desc: You were built to scout the edges of battle and outmaneuver your enemies. You are lean and designed for speed.

elements.name: Swift
elements.desc: Your walking speed is increased by 5 feet.

elements.name: Light Step
elements.desc: When you are traveling alone for an extended period of time (one hour or more), you can move stealthily at a normal pace.

elements.name: Sense Threats
elements.desc: You can cast the detect magic and detect poison and disease spells, but only as rituals. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

elements.name: Hunter's Intuition
elements.desc: Your mark sharpens your senses and helps you find your prey. When you make a Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Survival) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Imprint Prey
elements.desc: As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target is imprinted in your mind until it dies or you use this trait again. Alternatively, you can imprint a creature as your quarry whenever you succeed on a Wisdom (Survival) check to track it. When you are tracking your quarry, double the result of your Intuition die. When your quarry is within 60 feet of you, you have a general sense of its location. Your attacks against it ignore half cover. If you can’t see the target when you attack it, your inability to see it doesn’t impose disadvantage on the attack roll. Likewise, your quarry doesn’t doesn’t gain advantage on attack rolls against you due to being hidden or invisible. Once you use this trait, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

elements.name: Nature's Voice
elements.desc: When you reach 3rd level you gain the ability to cast locate animals or plants, but only as a ritual.

elements.desc: When you make a Wisdom (Animal Handling) or Intelligence (Nature) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Expert Handling
elements.desc: You can use the Help action to aid an ally animal companion or mount within 30 feet of you, rather than 5 feet of you.

elements.name: Primal Connection
elements.desc: You can cast animal friendship once with this trait and regain the ability to do so when you finish a short or long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

elements.name: The Bigger They Are
elements.desc: When you cast a spell that affects only beasts, it also affects monstrosities with an Intelligence score of 3 or lower.

elements.name: The Mark of Healing

elements.name: Medical Intuition
elements.desc: When you make a Wisdom (Medicine) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Healing Touch
elements.desc: As an action, you can draw power from your dragonmark to spend one of your Hit Dice and revitalize yourself or a creature you touch. Roll the die, add your Wisdom modifier, and the creature regains a number of hit points equal to the total. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

elements.name: The Mark of Hospitality
elements.desc: They may not always have gold, but a halfling with the Mark of Hospitality is sure to be rich in friends. The magic of the mark allows the bearer to keep a...

elements.name: Inkeeper’s Charm
elements.desc: You know the cantrips friends and prestidigitation Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them.

elements.name: Ever Hospitable
elements.desc: When you make a Charisma (Persuasion) check or an ability check involving brewer’s supplies or cook’s utensils, you can roll one Intuition die (a d4) and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: The Mark of Making
elements.desc: The Mark of Making guides its bearer through any act of creation. The bearer of the mark can mend broken things with a touch, and always has a minor magic...

elements.name: Artisan’s Intuition
elements.desc: When you make an ability check with artisan’s tools, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Maker’s Gift
elements.desc: You know the cantrip mending and gain proficiency with one type of artisan’s tools.

elements.name: Magecraft
elements.desc: You can create a temporary magic item out of common materials. Choose a cantrip from the wizard spell list. Describe the item connected to it. As long as you possess the item, you know that cantrip. At the end of a long rest, you can replace it with a new item and select a new cantrip from the wizard spell list. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these cantrips.

elements.name: Spellsmith
elements.desc: You can spend one minute to weave a temporary enchantment into a nonmagical suit of armor or weapon. For the next hour the object becomes a magic item, gaining a +1 bonus to AC if it is armor or a +1 bonus to hit and damage if it is a weapon. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

elements.name: The Mark of Passage
elements.desc: The Mark of Passage governs motion, allowing its bearer to move with uncanny speed and precision. Running, leaping, climbing—the Mark of Passage enhances...

elements.name: Intuitive Motion
elements.desc: When you make a Strength (Athletics) check or any ability check to operate or maintain a land vehicle, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Determined Stride
elements.desc: When you use the Dash action, difficult terrain doesn’t cost you extra movement on that turn.

elements.name: Shared Passage
elements.desc: As a bonus action you can teleport a distance up to your walking speed, ending in an unoccupied space that you can see. You can bring one willing creature of your size or smaller who is carrying gear up to its carrying capacity. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you use this trait. Once you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

elements.name: The Mark of Scribing
elements.desc: The Mark of Scribing deals with communication—both the written and spoken word. A gnome who bears the mark can feel words as though they are living...

elements.name: Gifted Scribe
elements.desc: You are proficient with calligrapher’s supplies and forgery kits. When you make an ability check using either one of these tools, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Scribe’s Insight
elements.desc: You can cast comprehend languages once with this trait and you regain the ability to do so after a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.

elements.name: Whispering Wind
elements.desc: You know the cantrip Message. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability when casting it.

elements.name: The Mark of Sentinel

elements.name: Sentinel’s Intuition
elements.desc: When you roll for Initiative or make a Wisdom (Perception) check to notice a threat, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add it to the ability check.

elements.name: Sentinel’s Shield
elements.desc: You know the cantrip blade ward. You can cast shield once with this trait and regain the ability to do so after you finish a short or long rest.

elements.name: Vigilant Guardian
elements.desc: As an action, you can designate an ally you can see as your ward. You have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) and Wisdom (Perception) checks made to spot threats to your ward. In addition, when you are within 5 feet of your ward, and that creature is the target of an attack that you can see, you can use your reaction to swap places with your ward. When you do, you become the target of the attack.

elements.name: The Mark of Shadow
elements.desc: The Mark of Shadows lets an elf weave illusions from shadows, crafting sounds and images to distract or delight. The mark also allows its bearer to draw on...

elements.name: Gift of The Shadow
elements.desc: When you make a Charisma (Performance) or Dexterity (Stealth) check, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Slip Into Shadow
elements.desc: You can use the Hide action as a bonus action, even if you have no cover or if you’re under observation. Regardless of whether you succeed or fail, once you use this you cannot use it again until after a short or long rest.

elements.name: Shape Shadow
elements.desc: You know the minor illusion cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this trait.

elements.name: The Mark of Storm
elements.desc: Wind and water welcome the half-elf who carries the Mark of Storm. The wind catches them when they fall, and they swim with remarkable speed. Those who...

elements.name: Windwright's Intuition
elements.desc: When you make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or any ability check involving operating or maintaining a water or air vehicle, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Storm’s Blessing
elements.desc: You have resistance to lightning damage.

elements.name: Headwinds
elements.desc: You know the gust cantrip. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the gust of wind spell once with this trait and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

elements.desc: The Mark of Warding helps its bearers protect things of value. Using the mark, a dwarf can weave wards and seal portals with mystic force. It also provides...

elements.name: Master of Locks
elements.desc: When you make an Intelligence (History), Intelligence (Investigation), or Thieves’ Tools check involving lock and trap mechanisms, you can roll one Intuition die, a d4, and add the number rolled to the ability check.

elements.name: Wards and Seals
elements.desc: You can use your mark to cast the alarm spell as a ritual. Starting at 3rd level you can cast arcane lock once with this trait and you regain the ability to do so after a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
